title: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision
venue: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 202, 28492–28518
access: Publisher full text; relevant methods, multilingual evaluation, and training statistics inspected. No replication.
method: Encoder–decoder Transformer trained with large-scale multilingual weak supervision; zero-shot benchmark evaluation.
findings: 680,000 training hours support broad zero-shot transfer; multilingual accuracy varies with language resources.
limitations: Web-data and language imbalance; benchmarks do not validate Kazakhstan sales calls or business-entity accuracy.
project_use: Reproducible ASR baseline; measure Kazakh, Russian, and mixed-language performance separately.
claim_locator: §§2.1–2.3; §3.4 and Figure 3; Appendix G/Figure 10; bibliography year follows ICML 2023, not preprint 2022.
verification_note: Primary publication record and relevant full-text sections rechecked; no experimental replication.

title: WhisperX: Time-Accurate Speech Transcription of Long-Form Audio
access: Publisher full text; pipeline, benchmarks, ablations, and multilingual caveat inspected. No replication.
method: Voice activity detection, cut-and-merge segmentation, batched Whisper, and forced phoneme alignment.
findings: Improves benchmark word timing and long-form transcription; batching accelerates the tested configuration.
limitations: Alignment needs suitable language models; non-English word segmentation lacked quantitative evaluation.
project_use: Timestamp evidence spans for sales facts; validate multilingual timing and local throughput.
claim_locator: Figure 1; §2.5 and footnote 2; §3.4; Tables 2–3. Reported speedups are experimental, not deployment guarantees.
verification_note: Primary publication record and relevant full-text sections rechecked; no experimental replication.

title: pyannote.audio 2.1 speaker diarization pipeline: principle, benchmark, and recipe
access: Publisher full text; pipeline, 11-benchmark table, and adaptation recipe inspected. No replication.
method: Local speaker segmentation, embeddings, and global clustering; domain adaptation experiments.
findings: Diarization quality varies across domains; segmentation fine-tuning often improves out-of-domain results.
limitations: Telephone and difficult acoustic domains retain substantial errors; benchmark scoring conventions affect comparisons.
project_use: Separate salesperson/customer turns; require DER evaluation and role-label confirmation.
claim_locator: §§2–4; Table 1; no-collar, overlap-inclusive scoring in §3; CALLHOME results in Table 1.
verification_note: Primary publication record and relevant full-text sections rechecked; no experimental replication.

title: KSC2: An Industrial-Scale Open-Source Kazakh Speech Corpus
access: Publisher full text; corpus composition, splitting, ASR setup, and results inspected. No replication.
method: Multi-source Kazakh corpus with Russian code-switching; Transformer streaming-ASR validation.
findings: Overall test WER is 15.6%; reported spontaneous subsets range from 27.0% to 36.8%, exposing domain sensitivity.
limitations: Not a sales-call corpus; speaker overlap between splits is not fully excluded.
project_use: Kazakh comparison baseline and code-switching rationale; create separate business-call evaluation.
verification_note: Primary publication record and relevant full-text sections rechecked; no experimental replication.

title: An End-to-End Dialogue Summarization System for Sales Calls
venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies: Industry Track, 45–53
access: Publisher landing page and published full text inspected on 22 October 2026, including architecture, experiments, metric disagreement, and conclusions. No replication.
method: Segment sales-call transcripts; summarize with speaker/turn-aware DialogBART; filter grammatical acceptability; permit human editing. GPT-3 supplies offline pseudo-labels.
findings: Human-plus-pseudo-label training improves tested ROUGE scores. In the DialogSum comparison, pseudo-only training scores higher on ROUGE but lower on automatic FactCC than human-only training.
limitations: Only 100 proprietary test examples; no demonstrated Russian/Kazakh transfer or causal productivity lift. Grammatical acceptability filtering does not establish faithfulness to audio.
project_use: Justify editable, speaker-aware call highlights and human review; evaluate factual grounding separately from fluency and lexical overlap.
claim_locator: §3 architecture/DialogBART/acceptability; §6.1/Table 2 (500 DialogSum, 819 SAMSum, 100 proprietary test samples); §6.3/Figure 6 (DialogSum ROUGE versus automatic FactCC); proceedings pp.45–53.
verification_note: Primary publication record and relevant full-text sections rechecked; no experimental replication.

title: QMSum: A New Benchmark for Query-based Multi-domain Meeting Summarization
access: Publisher full text; query annotations, locate-then-summarize method, and evaluation inspected. No replication.
method: 1,808 query-summary pairs over 232 meetings; relevant-span retrieval followed by summarization.
findings: Locating relevant spans improves selected baselines; long-context retrieval and synthesis remain challenging.
limitations: Meeting domains differ from sales; benchmark ROUGE does not establish financial-fact correctness.
project_use: Retrieve evidence for objections, commitments, and next actions before generating summaries.
verification_note: Primary publication record and relevant full-text sections rechecked; no experimental replication.

title: CONFIT: Toward Faithful Dialogue Summarization with Linguistically-Informed Contrastive Fine-tuning
access: Publisher full text; error taxonomy, training method, and human-evaluation tables inspected. No replication.
method: Contrastive fine-tuning with factual-error negatives and dialogue-specific self-supervised loss.

title: Careless Whisper: Speech-to-Text Hallucination Harms
venue: Proceedings of the 2024 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency, 1672–1681
access: Author-deposited full text rechecked on 23 October 2026, including methods, temporal retest, results and limitations. ACM/DOI publisher pages returned HTTP 403 during this recheck; publication identity and DOI also appear in the manuscript front matter. No replication.
method: Repeated 2023 API transcription of AphasiaBank audio; manual hallucination verification and thematic coding.
findings: Historical experiments found invented phrases; silence patterns and speaker characteristics are associated with risk.
limitations: Specialized English sample and changing 2023 API; reported rates are not current sales-call estimates. Detection can miss hallucinations repeated identically across runs.
project_use: Audit silence and unsupported text; retain audio evidence and review consequential extracted claims.
claim_locator: §§2.1–2.5; §3 including December retest; §3.1 limitations. Do not generalize the 1.4% historical rate.
verification_note: Author manuscript rechecked; direct publisher access returned HTTP 403. Proceedings identity retained; no replication.

title: AI-assisted sales coaching framework: Empirically-derived models for B2B communication analysis
access: Open-access published PDF available in University of Turku repository; inspected methods, results, and limitations. Available online 23 March 2026.
method: Design-science framework using 5,183 Finnish B2B calls; combines acoustic, semantic, and linguistic features, conversation graphs, temporal classifiers, and SHAP explanations.
findings: Reports temporal prediction AUC 0.784 with a broad WON definition. Its 0.957 rejection analysis classifies an engineered risk category among unsuccessful calls, not actual sales outcomes.
limitations: Finnish organization and broad WON label; engineered rejection target overlaps risk input features, raising circularity concerns. Progression efficiency formula and Table 1 scale need reconciliation. No controlled deployment-effect evidence.
project_use: Use as an architectural precedent; independently define outcomes and leakage controls. Do not copy the rejection AUC as a sales-performance target.
claim_locator: Sections 3.1 and 3.4; Table 1; Sections 4.3 and 4.4. Rejection subset includes 4929 unsuccessful calls; composite target differs from an independently observed sale.
verification_note: Official repository metadata and indexed primary full-text passages rechecked; direct PDF returned HTTP 403. No replication.

title: Annotating Customer-Oriented Behaviour in Call Centre Sales Dialogues
access: Open full text; inspected corpus, annotation experiments, ratings analysis, and limitations. Author order here follows authoritative PDF; ACL landing-page order is Stock, Petukhova, Klakow.
method: ISO 24617-2 dialogue-act annotation with relationship-building extensions and DIT++ feedback analysis on 67 German service/sales calls (4.3 hours).
findings: Relationship-building annotations associate with customer ratings; feedback acts provide contextual evidence for analysing sales negotiation.
limitations: Small deliberately selected German corpus with experienced agents and favourable rating bias; correlations with satisfaction do not prove conversion improvement.
project_use: Create auditable labels for needs discovery, offers, commitments, feedback, and relationship-building, with timestamps and annotated evidence.
claim_locator: PDF p.1 author order; Sections 4.1–4.3 corpus, rating-selection bias and annotation; Section 5 German/inbound-context limitations. No DOI listed in ACL record.
verification_note: Primary publication record and relevant full-text sections rechecked; no experimental replication.

title: Entity-level Sentiment Analysis in Contact Center Telephone Conversations
access: Open published PDF; inspected methods and experimental results. Metadata pagination is 484–491 while PDF prints 494–501; avoid silently treating these as identical.
method: English contact-centre entity sentiment and opinion-word extraction using DistilBERT variants versus CNN plus linguistic heuristics.

title: Determining the quality of B2C sales leads from online chats
venue: International Journal of Research in Marketing, 43(2), 383–403
access: Publisher abstract, highlights, and study/data section snippets inspected; full text requires subscription and was not read. Cite 2026 issue year; DOI reflects 2025 online publication.
method: Sales-manager qualitative research, automotive chat topic/predictive analysis, and replication in furniture; links conversation text with downstream purchase and profit.
findings: Proposes MINITS: Mode of contact, Immediacy, Need, Interest, Time spent chatting and Specificity; conversational signals help qualify leads.

project_use: Specify interpretable lead features and connect transcript-derived signals to CRM purchase/profit outcomes rather than using sentiment as the sole target.
claim_locator: Publisher abstract/highlights; Overview of studies; Data/sample snippets for automotive and furniture. Publisher issue metadata: June 2026, volume 43(2), pages 383–403.

title: Drivers of industrial sales performance in the agent-buyer chat channel: The role of social and functional content, message valence, and synchronicity
venue: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services, 78, Article 103774
access: Publisher abstract, introduction, methods/results snippets, and CRediT author names inspected; full text not accessed.
method: Observational regression analysis of message content, valence, response time, and word proportions in Brazilian automotive-parts B2B chats; 19,817 conversations over 714 days.

title: Resistance in Business-to-Business “Cold” Sales Calls
venue: Journal of Language and Social Psychology, 42(5–6), 630–652
access: Open publisher full text; inspected Data and Method, examples, and discussion; publisher PDF verifies final pagination.
method: Discursive psychology and conversation analysis of 159 authentic British B2B cold calls from four companies; detailed analysis of 12 blocks and 14 stalls.
findings: Distinguishes resistance that attempts to terminate selling (blocks) from resistance that delays progress (stalls), using conversational sequence and context.
limitations: Qualitative findings concern appointment seeking, not automated classifier accuracy or completed-sale prediction; calls recorded in 2014–2016.
project_use: Design objection labels that distinguish rejection from postponement and retain adjacent turns, timing, and uncertainty for human review.
claim_locator: Publisher Abstract; Data and Method; Results sections on blocks and stalls; final issue metadata 42(5–6), 630–652.
